b: More stories from fictional Breadminster by the UK-based digital riddim stylist

The last track on Elijah Minnelli’s new album is called ‘Contested Estuary’, a Stockholm-syndrome-inducing track, vaguely based on the old Appalachian ballad, ‘Vandy’. Setting the scene with the hypnotic tones of a singing bowl, Minnelli intones a song about a loyal woman who awaits her husband’s return from war, rejecting the advances of a wealthy suitor in the meantime. As the narrative unfolds, the beat and sinister double bass unravel, accompanied by the sounds of crackling wood that conjure up the bow test in the latest Christopher Nolan film.​Eventually, Minelli shifts focus from the addressee (Vandy) to the suitor.
